r.정치 구도: A parliamentary system in which parliament chooses the prime minister. Since the 2003 US invasion toppled the dictatorship, a convention has taken hold: the prime minister is a Shia, the largest group, the president a Kurd and the speaker of parliament a Sunni. Because posts are divided by sect and ethnicity, ministries and state companies tend to become party fiefdoms, and many blame the system for widespread corruption. The largest bloc is an alliance of Shia parties, some of which command armed groups close to Iran. The militias that gathered in 2014 to fight the Islamic State became part of the state's security forces, but many units act on their own, and bringing all weapons under state control is a major challenge. After the November 2025 election, government formation dragged on until a new prime minister won a confidence vote in May 2026, and the cabinet was completed only in October. The Kurdistan Regional Government in the north has its own forces and parliament and often clashes with Baghdad over oil sales and budget shares.

t.why: One of the biggest producers in OPEC, it relies on crude exports for most of its state revenue. Most of its exports leave by tanker from Basra in the south and pass through the Strait of Hormuz, so when the 2026 war between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other, which began in February, disrupted shipping through the strait, exports plunged. Baghdad has since restarted the pipeline from Kirkuk in the north to the Turkish port of Ceyhan and is looking for new pipeline routes. It shares a long border and religious ties with Iran, so balancing between Washington and Tehran sits at the heart of its foreign policy. When the Islamic State swept across the north and west in 2014, a US-led coalition came in to fight alongside Iraqi forces; that mission ended in September 2026 and US troops withdrew. Dams built upstream by Turkey and Iran have reduced the flow of the Tigris and Euphrates, making water shortages a serious problem.
t.rel: Caught between Iran and the United States, where both countries' influence overlaps. It has a Kurdish autonomous region in the north and disputes with Turkey over water and Kurdish militants.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in July 1989. From 2004 to 2008 the Korean Zaytun Division was stationed in Erbil, in the Kurdistan region, helping with reconstruction. Iraq is one of Korea's major sources of crude oil. Hanwha is building Bismayah New City, a 100,000-home development near Baghdad, and Daewoo E&C has been working on the new Al Faw port in the south. The Bismayah project, however, has run into repeated trouble, including a halt in 2022 when payments fell behind.
t.know: The ancient city of Babylon, famous for its Hanging Gardens, is in Iraq and became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2019.
etext: Its crude reserves are among the five largest in the world, and shallow fields keep production costs low. Oil makes up most exports and around 90% of government revenue. Output is capped by quotas set jointly by OPEC, Russia and other producers.

Much of the gas that comes up with crude oil is simply flared. Meanwhile it buys gas and electricity for its power plants from Iran, and blackouts and protests return every summer. Capturing the wasted gas is seen as its most urgent task.

Cities, roads and housing destroyed by war and the fight against the Islamic State still need rebuilding. The flagship plan is the Development Road, a rail and road corridor from the southern port of Al Faw to the Turkish border.

A huge public payroll means salaries and pensions take up a large share of the budget, while private-sector jobs are scarce. When oil prices fall or export routes are blocked, money to pay salaries quickly runs short. Corruption and restrictions on dollar transactions also deter investment.
